comment: Whole-product and indication-level withdrawals verified from sources opened on 13 November 2026 (Europe/Paris). Only whole-product entries remove a drug from Mainstream. Indication-level entries are reported by the gate and must not silently drop a drug that still has another approved use.

entries.detail: FDA withdrew approval of NDA 215310 for EXKIVITY (mobocertinib succinate) capsule, effective 15 July 2024, after Takeda asked for withdrawal. Takeda announced on 2 October 2023 that it would work with the FDA towards a voluntary withdrawal. The EMA application was withdrawn earlier, on 20 July 2022; that is a different event (the EU marketing application, not a US approval withdrawal).

indication_level_noted.indication: In combination with cetuximab for KRAS G12C mutated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy.
indication_level_noted.sure: Confirmed from the FDA Prior Approval sNDA letter for NDA 216340/S-011, electronically signed 1 September 2026 (Reference ID 5862281; Europe/Paris), which approves voluntary withdrawal of the accelerated colorectal-cancer indication (in combination with cetuximab; PMR 4650-1). Also listed on the FDA Withdrawn Cancer Accelerated Approvals page opened on 13 November 2026 (Europe/Paris), with Withdrawal Date 9/1/2026. A Federal Register API search of 2026 FDA “Withdrawal of Approval” notices through 13 November 2026 found no matching entry for adagrasib, Krazati, or NDA 216340. The NSCLC indication is a different use and is not treated as withdrawn.

indication_level_noted.indication: As monotherapy for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after failure of platinum-based and docetaxel chemotherapy (accelerated approval 5/5/2003, withdrawal date 4/25/2012).
indication_level_noted.sure: Confirmed from Federal Register notice 2012-9944, published 25 April 2012 (Effective 25 April 2012), opened 13 November 2026 (Europe/Paris). The notice withdraws NDA 21-399, whose indication was monotherapy after failure of platinum-based and docetaxel chemotherapies. Gefitinib later has a different FDA label use (first-line EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R) which remains in this snapshot and is not treated as withdrawn.
indication_level_noted.plain: Its older use after chemotherapy was withdrawn in the US in 2012; first-treatment use is still approved.

sources.label: Federal Register notice 2012-9944 (77 FR 24723)
sources.detail: Opened 13 November 2026 (Europe/Paris). Effective 25 April 2012. FDA withdrew approval of NDA 21-399 for IRESSA (gefitinib) Tablets. The withdrawn indication, as stated in the notice, was monotherapy after failure of both platinum-based and docetaxel chemotherapies for locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (accelerated approval 2 May 2003). The current FDA label in this snapshot has a later, different first-treatment use that is not treated as withdrawn.
